topic: safe prefix reuse
canonical_claim: Bumping writer generation and rejecting old-format startup does not quiesce an already-running old writer that continues writing a reused prefix without reopening it Pool recreation is refused while a live mount lease of any format generation exists; after the owner is terminalized, the recreated pool claims normally and a delayed old-writer write is fenced out. Prefix reuse requires enforced quiescence, terminal-owner checks, normal-claim fencing on reuse, and a delayed old-writer refusal integration test A format-generation migration must bump both the writer generation and backward floor, update version goldens, and require quiesced recreation so an old writer cannot touch the reused prefix. Prefix recreation requires a fresh prefix or exact owner and lease terminalization plus writer drain before reuse

topic: recreate-only pre-release formats
canonical_claim: CAS is pre-release in this plan, so adding metas and removing the blob envelope requires recreating existing development pools; no migration, dual read/write path, or compatibility configuration is retained. Migration is recreate-only: pool format generations and backward floors advance together, old-format startup fails closed at pool open, and no dual reader or in-place converter is provided. The Stage A pool format writer generation and backward floor are bumped together; opening an old format fails closed with a message directing the operator to recreate the pool. The layout transition to opaque `life_id` keys is a recreate-only generation-6 cut, and the removal lifecycle's `_cleanup` deletion and `ref_lives` fold-seal transition is a separate recreate-only generation-7 wire cut; older generations are refused rather than dual-read or migrated. The existing format-bump-B recreate-only migration remains in force, and legacy unqualified ref and `_files` keys are rejected. CAS pool layout changes from v3 metadata are handled by recreating development pools; there is no migration, compatibility scaffolding, dual read path, or configuration flag. The all-tree CAS change is pre-release and does not add compatibility scaffolding; pools are recreated and ref-log and snapshot payload formats may change freely. The generation-6 opaque-life layout cut and generation-7 unified ref-life wire cut are recreate-only format boundaries with no compatibility parser, copy-forward path, or fallback that reinterprets older name-keyed objects as current life-keyed files. The pre-release pool format does not owe compatibility scaffolding or a dual protocol; a format bump is preferred because no persisted production data exists.; Existing pre-release or soak pools require a quiesced format bump and recreation; startup against the old format must fail closed with a message naming pool recreation, while any preservation requires a separate offline migration protocol.

topic: The carve interface is `utils/cas-carve/carve
canonical_claim: The carve interface is `utils/cas-carve/carve.sh [--src <ref>] [--base <ref>] [--branch <name>] [--check] [--force]`, defaulting to `HEAD`, `altinity/antalya-26.6`, and `cas-carved`.

topic: The carve classifier processes EXCLUDES before ordered GROUPS, uses firs
canonical_claim: The carve classifier processes EXCLUDES before ordered GROUPS, uses first-match-wins classification, hard-fails with the complete unmatched-file list, and warns rather than failing when a group matches zero files.; The carve script must hard-fail on an unmatched diff file, a completeness-invariant violation, or an existing target branch without `--force`; an empty group is warning-only, and the script must not use sleep-style waiting or push.

topic: carve apply worktree
canonical_claim: The carve apply phase creates a temporary worktree at `tmp/carve-worktree` from `git merge-base $BASE $SRC`, checks out or removes each classified source file in manifest order, and commits each non-empty group with its group message. The planned apply phase uses `git worktree add -b $BRANCH $WT $MB`, commits each group with `git commit -F -`, and removes the temporary worktree on exit while retaining the branch.

topic: carve completeness check
canonical_claim: The carve completeness invariant requires `git diff <branch>..$SRC --name-only` restricted by the exclude pathspecs to be empty; the script prints unrestricted differences as the discarded report summarized by exclude category. The planned completeness check compares `git diff --name-only --no-renames HEAD $SRC_SHA`, counts only paths matching EXCLUDES as discarded, and reports every non-excluded difference as a lost file before failing.

topic: carve test-file classification
canonical_claim: Within `tests/queries/0_stateless/`, added files belong to the new CAS stateless-test group and modified files belong to the old-test-tag group; this requires `--name-status` plus `added-only` and `modified-only` path matching. The carve stateless-test group matches only added files under `tests/queries/`, while the CI/tag group matches only modified files under that tree; this prevents new tests and old-test tag edits from sharing a commit.
